rule.description: One shared record-capability protocol (at least four capability members) is adopted across record owners and helper signatures that individually use only a fraction of it; measurement of which protocol members each owner reads, writes, or overrides identifies every forced manifestation.

checks.description: Detect record owners that are forced to accept a shared capability protocol whose members they never use.
checks.detected_relation: record owner -> unused members of an adopted capability protocol
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: The record interface exceeds every adopter's dependency boundary: each helper family owns records whose observable responsibilities are narrow, yet adoption universalizes one capability set over all of them.

checks.description: Detect one ambient record protocol documented as the surface of many helper signatures whose implementations use only parts of it.
checks.detected_relation: helper signature -> fat shared record protocol spanning unrelated helper families
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: A single interface with several capability groups is propagated through unrelated helper boundaries, so consumers and implementors of each helper see and depend on capabilities belonging to other families.

excluded.reason: The module-directory re-exports the helper functions by name; it introduces no record protocol of its own, so no capability boundary is defined there.

These construct import-interop records whose members are copied structurally from a module namespace; they enumerate no capability members and forcing them into a capability protocol would require behavioral extension, not consequence-free surface widening.

The records they handle are locked-down value wrappers (a frozen array, a one-field box, WeakMap states); none has a multi-capability surface that could be widened without changing observable behavior.

These are the remaining helper families that keep no per-record surface at all for their emit-site (they consume functions, arrays, or primitive arguments), so there is no record owner to force a protocol onto.
